claim: Let \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) be a finite connected complete multipartite graph with \(r\ge2\). Then \(G\) is packing-total chromatic critical—meaning \(\chi_\rho^{\prime\prime}(H)<\chi_\rho^{\prime\prime}(G)\) for every proper subgraph \(H\subsetneq G\)—if and only if \(G\not\cong K_{n,1,1}\) for every integer \(n\ge2\). For the exceptional family, if \(e\) is the edge joining the two singleton parts, then \(G-e\cong K_{n,2}\) and \(\chi_\rho^{\prime\prime}(G-e)=\chi_\rho^{\prime\prime}(G)=2n+3\).
integrity: The universal classification is proved analytically. Finite computation is used only as a stress test and is not treated as a proof of the infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is limited to finite connected complete multipartite graphs.

The auxiliary exact value of the packing total chromatic number is not asserted to be independently novel, because older total-independence and edge-domination results cover closely related numerical information.
Only the abstract of arXiv:2609.10107 was available in the accessible comparison route; this is retained as a residual overlap risk.
title: Packing-total criticality of complete multipartite graphs
